crude-irn.text: Customs data record no crude oil exports from Iran in 2024, against 88.9 Mt in 2018 (CEPII BACI). From 2019 to 2022, 75.4 Mt of them were recorded under "Other Asia, not elsewhere specified" and are shown as "Asia, not specified". Unrecorded shipments, or cargoes declared under other origins, are a plausible cause; it is not established here.

crude-ven.text: Customs data record 21.7 Mt of crude oil exports from Venezuela in 2024, against 60.3 Mt in 2018 (CEPII BACI). Unrecorded shipments, or cargoes declared under other origins, are a plausible cause; it is not established here.

crude-mys.text: Crude oil exports of Malaysia in customs data (54.2 Mt in 2024, CEPII BACI) are 227% of its production (23.9 Mt, EIA International Energy Data). Blending, or crude of other origins declared as Malaysian after ship-to-ship transfers, is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

crude-are.text: Crude oil exports of the United Arab Emirates in customs data (184 Mt in 2024, CEPII BACI) are 100% of its production (183 Mt, EIA International Energy Data). 24.5 Mt of these exports are Atlas estimates from declared value. Crude of other origins loaded or blended in the country and declared as Emirati is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

crude-mex-s19.text: Crude oil from Mexico to "Other Asia, not elsewhere specified" (BACI code S19), shown here as Taiwan: 2.78 Mt in 2018, 13.1 Mt in 2019, 12.7 Mt in 2020, 15.2 Mt in 2021, 9.99 Mt in 2022, 8.43 Mt in 2023, 7.88 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI). No source read for the atlas confirms the destination.

crude-rus-tur.text: No crude oil from Russia to Turkey is recorded in customs data for 2022 to 2024 (4.2 Mt in 2021, CEPII BACI). Incomplete declarations by both sides may be the cause; it is not established here.

crude-kwt-vnm.text: No crude oil from Kuwait to Vietnam is recorded in customs data for 2024 (9.01 Mt in 2023, CEPII BACI). Incomplete declarations by both sides may be the cause; it is not established here.

crude-kwt.text: Customs data record 49.4 Mt of crude oil exports from Kuwait in 2024, against an average of 89.1 Mt a year from 2021 to 2023 (CEPII BACI). Of the buyers recorded in 2023, Vietnam (9.01 Mt) and Oman (2.48 Mt) are not recorded in 2024 (2 buyers, 11.5 Mt in 2023). Its crude oil production in the EIA International Energy Data file is 2,549 thousand barrels a day in 2024 against 2,679 in 2023. A gap in the importers' declarations for 2024, or a change in the recorded origin of the cargoes, is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

grain-rus-wheat.text: Customs data record 34.5 Mt of wheat exports from Russia in 2024 (CEPII BACI), of which 11.6 Mt is an Atlas estimate (the tonnage computed by the atlas from the declared value where the declared tonnage was implausible: Egypt 11.1 Mt, Nigeria 0.55 Mt) and 22.9 Mt is as reported; USDA PSD gives 55.5 Mt for 2023/24 and 43 Mt for 2024/25. These flows may rest on importers' declarations alone, so that destinations which do not report are missing; this is not established here. The published customs figure is 38% below the first and 20% below the second. On the tonnage as reported alone (22.9 Mt) the gap is 59% below the first and 47% below the second. Importers that took wheat from Russia in 2019 to 2021 and have none recorded in 2024: Bangladesh (1.75 Mt a year on average), Iran (1.24 Mt a year on average), Sudan (1 Mt a year on average), Yemen (0.93 Mt a year on average), DR Congo (0.548 Mt a year on average); the flows and lanes to them are zero in 2024. The flows and lanes carry the customs figures (an Atlas estimate is marked as such); no further tonnage is added to bring them to the USDA figure.

grain-rus-corn.text: Customs data record 2.24 Mt of corn exports from Russia in 2024 (CEPII BACI), of which 0.0212 Mt is an Atlas estimate (the tonnage computed by the atlas from the declared value where the declared tonnage was implausible: Lebanon 0.0163 Mt, Israel 0.00491 Mt) and 2.22 Mt is as reported; USDA PSD gives 6.6 Mt for 2023/24 and 3 Mt for 2024/25. These flows may rest on importers' declarations alone, so that destinations which do not report are missing; this is not established here. The published customs figure is 66% below the first and 25% below the second. On the tonnage as reported alone (2.22 Mt) the gap is 66% below the first and 26% below the second. Importers that took corn from Russia in 2019 to 2021 and have none recorded in 2024: Iran (0.917 Mt a year on average); the flows and lanes to them are zero in 2024. The flows and lanes carry the customs figures (an Atlas estimate is marked as such); no further tonnage is added to bring them to the USDA figure.

urea-irn.text: Urea exports of Iran in customs data fell from 3.77 Mt in 2019 to 0.024 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI). A change in the recorded origin of shipments is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

urea-omn.text: Urea exports of Oman in customs data (7.63 Mt in 2024, CEPII BACI) are 178% of its production in the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (2 Mt of nitrogen in 2024); urea exports converted to nitrogen with the nitrogen content of urea (0.4665, from molar masses), against ammonia production in nitrogen content. Declaration of cargoes of other origins under Oman is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

potash-blr.text: Potash exports of Belarus in customs data fell from 11.6 Mt in 2020 to 3.59 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI). A change in the recorded origin of shipments is a plausible cause; it is not established here. Of the 11.6 Mt of potash that Belarus exported through Russia in 2025, 9% went by rail to China and the CIS countries together and the rest through Russian seaports, half of it from Bronka (Kommersant, as reported by Reform.news on 27 March 2026, https://reform.news/en/belarus-exported-11-6-million-tonnes-of-potash-fertilizers-via-russian-ports). The atlas counts Belarus's recorded potash exports to China as seaborne, through St Petersburg: the page gives no rail share for China alone, so nothing is subtracted.

potash-uzb.text: Potash exports of Uzbekistan in customs data rose from 0.158 Mt in 2022 to 1.76 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI); the country is not a listed producer in the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries. A change in the recorded origin of shipments is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

lpg-omn-chn.text: Customs data record 2.75 Mt of LPG from Oman to China in 2024 (86% of its recorded exports, CEPII BACI). The origin of these cargoes is not checked against an independent source: while Iran's exports are unrecorded, cargoes of other origins declared under Oman may account for part of this volume; it is not established here, and the atlas has no free source to measure it.

uv-aluminium-USA-MYS.text: Unwrought aluminium (HS 7601) from the United States to Malaysia: 0.536 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI), declared at 1,034 USD per tonne, 40% of the tonne-weighted median of the group (2,565); the 2024 average aluminium price is 2,419 USD per tonne (World Bank Pink Sheet), and the pair is declared at 43% of it. Material priced like scrap or alloy, or another cheaper product, declared under this code is a plausible cause; it is not established here.
